definition: Structure mining or structured data mining is the process of finding and extracting useful information from semi-structured data sets.
details: Graph mining, sequential pattern mining and molecule mining are special cases of structured data mining.

explainer.lead: Finding and extracting useful information from semi-structured data sets. It matters because much real-world data is neither fully free text nor cleanly tabulated.

tiers.eli5: Instead of reading every sentence, you look at how the data is arranged—links between things, orders of steps—to pull out what you need.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to data with implicit organization, such as graphs or sequences; the pitfall is that semi-structured data's inconsistent form makes extraction rules fragile.
tiers.paperLevel: Structure mining, or structured data mining, extracts information from semi-structured data sets; graph mining, sequential pattern mining and molecule mining are special cases.

explainer.example: Mining a molecule data set to extract useful information is treated as a case of structured data mining.
